summary: 1934 Forest Service fire tower in Bath County, KY; cab burned in an arson fire in 2008, tower closed, restoration still short of funds.

facts.design: 35-foot steel tower with a wood cab; cab rebuilt in 1959 on a structure half the original height (one source only)
facts.status_note: Steel tower stands, but the wood cab was destroyed by fire in 2008 and has since been taken off; the platform has a hole in it and the structure is judged unsafe for visitors.

access.note: Closed to the public and judged unsafe for visitors, per the Forest Service statement quoted by NHLR and per LEX18.

events.note: Constructed by the Forest Service in 1934; erected as a 35-foot steel tower with wood cab by the Civilian Conservation Corps
Cab rebuilt on a structure half the original height, per the Eastern lookouts history only
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register May 29, 1993
Arson fire on December 3, 2008 destroyed the wood cab; a local news report (KY News Group) says vandals did it
Brent Frizzell, former Salt Lick fire chief, involved in the restoration project since 2017
Received a $75,000 grant (LEX18 gives 2023; KY News Group says the county was awarded it in 2024)
Local, state and federal officials met at the tower with the Tater Knob Restoration Group (KY News Group report dated September 17, 2026)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: An NHLR visitor comment says the tower is operated as a scenic lookout. The Forest Service statement on the same page and the LEX18 and KY News Group reports say it is closed and unsafe. The story follows the closed status.
LEX18 dates the $75,000 grant to 2023; KY News Group says the county was awarded it in 2024. The story reports both dates and does not pick one.
The Forest Service statement and the Eastern lookouts history call the fire arson. KY News Group says vandals burned the cab. The story reports both accounts.

notes_for_editor: Elevation not in facts. The brief gives 384.4 m, but LEX18 says the highest point in Bath County is 1,388 feet (about 423 m); the two should be checked against a survey before either is used. The 1959 rebuild comes from one source (Eastern lookouts history) and is worded as 'half the original height' without detail. The tower 'fell out of use in the 1970s' is a decade only, so no event year is given. NHLR 'Staffed? No' is undated, so staffing as_of uses the check date. The USFS recarea page in the brief (recid=70728) does not mention Tater Knob, so the 2008 Forest Service statement is taken from its quotation on NHLR. Read budget ran over (about 7 page reads) because the first two fetches were low-yield.
